forecaster_note: Size comes back up as the mid-period swell eases further but new longer-period S swell fills in and helps out. Solid surf in the head to overhead range for south-swell-favouring breaks. Less exposed spots should see slow sets wrapping in at around head high, sheltered corners much smaller. Offshore winds early give a window of decent conditions before NE sea breezes in the afternoon mean all but S-facing breaks go onshore and lumpy. — Surfline forecast team

wind.summary: Light NW offshore till mid-morning, then NE sea breeze 15–23 km/h from midday

shark.summary: SharkSmart check pending this refresh — tap to check live detections

days.label: Today
days.note: Get up and go. Light NW offshore holds until roughly 11am, then the NE sea breeze swings on at 15 km/h and trashes everything except the S-facing corners. Swell is dominated by long-period S (182–186°, 12–18s) — that's the wrap Dee Why hates, so Long Reef and Curl Curl are the picks today.

dee-why.window: 6:00–10:30am while the NW offshore holds. Chest-high sets, inconsistent at 47%.
alerts: Dead S swell at 182° wraps badly here — expect soft, gutless sets between the good ones

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: The Point is your frontside wall but the S direction won't light it up. Sit wide on the bank and be patient — 47% consistency means long lulls then a set of three.

long-reef.window: 6:00–11:00am. Best of the four — takes the S swell square on and the NW is straight offshore.

tip.label: Pick of the day
tip.text: Chest to overhead with 272 kJ behind it. Step up a touch — this is the one that'll have real push. Wind goes cross by noon, so don't sleep in.

curl-curl.window: 6:00–11:00am before the NE onshore at midday.

tip.label: Backside at the south end
tip.text: South corner banks will be holding the S swell cleanest. Chest to head and punchy — your favourite size range if the banks cooperate.

manly.window: 6:00–9:00am only — goes cross-shore early and POOR by afternoon.
alerts: Most sheltered of the four — S swell barely gets in, half the size of Long Reef

tip.label: Skip it today
tip.text: Thigh to waist while Long Reef is chest to overhead. Only worth it if you want an easy longboard paddle.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Cleaner but smaller and dropping fast. Dawn is the whole session — NW offshore till about 9am, then it swings NE and builds to 22–30 km/h by mid-afternoon. Long Reef again holds the most size.

dee-why.window: 6:00–8:30am. Drops to thigh-stomach after that and the wind ruins it.
alerts: Energy halves overnight — 272 kJ down to 125 kJ

long-reef.window: 6:00–11:00am. Clean chest-to-head with NW offshore — the best window of the weekend for shape.

curl-curl.window: 6:00–9:00am, then cross-shore and fading to POOR.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Both days are early-session weekends: NW offshore at dawn, NE sea breeze from late morning. Saturday has the energy (272 kJ), Sunday has the cleaner shape but half the power. Long Reef is the call both mornings. Past the weekend the S swell keeps easing into Monday — grab it now.

dee-why.window: Sat 6–10:30am is the stronger of the two mornings.
alerts: S-dominant swell both days — not Dee Why's direction

long-reef.window: Sat 6–11am for size, Sun 6–11am for shape. Either works.

curl-curl.window: Saturday morning is clearly the better of the two here.

manly.window: Dawn only, both days. Smallest of the four all weekend.
alerts: Too sheltered for this S swell
